title: Leader Election
explain: Leader election picks exactly one node to do a job that must not run twice at once, such as accepting writes for a shard or running the scheduler. The goal is easy; the danger is split brain, two leaders at the same time, so the real question is how you make sure the old one is out. I also say that if the work can be partitioned, you may not need a leader at all.
model:
Three ways to elect, from strongest to weakest:

1. **Built into [consensus](#/sd/f/consensus)**: [Raft](#/sd/f/raft)-style majority votes with numbered terms. Safe under partitions; this is what etcd and ZooKeeper give you.
2. **Lease on a coordinator**: every candidate tries one conditional write (create-if-absent, compare-and-set) with a TTL. The winner is leader and must keep renewing. It is a [lease](#/sd/f/lease), so leadership moves when renewals stop.
3. **ID- or clock-based self-declaration** ("lowest reachable id wins"): simple, but each side of a partition elects its own leader.

```
leader renews --X-- (pause / partition) ... lease expires ... standby wins, token+1
old leader wakes up, still believes it leads --> resource rejects its stale token
```

A deposed leader may not know it yet, so safety comes from a [fencing token](#/sd/f/fencing-token) (term or lease epoch) checked by the resource, not from the leader's belief. Election time is downtime: detection plus lease, with no leader in between.

details.q: Why can't the leader just check 'am I still the leader?' before each write?
details.a: Because the check and the write are not atomic and the leader may be paused between them (GC, a stalled network). By the time it writes, someone else may hold leadership. Only the resource can refuse stale writes, using a fencing token.

details.q: What is the worst-case time without a leader in a lease-based scheme?
details.a: Roughly the lease TTL after the last renewal plus how often standbys poll. Example: 15 s TTL and standbys polling every 2 s gives up to about 17 s with no leader. Shorter TTL means faster failover but more false failovers.

details.q: Why do Raft-style systems randomize election timeouts?
details.a: Identical timeouts make every follower campaign at once and split the votes forever. Random timers let one candidate collect a majority before the others start.

It relies on each node seeing the others. In a partition each side sees a different lowest id and elects its own leader, so both accept writes. A majority or a CAS in a consensus-backed store cannot be won by both sides.

details.q: A leader holds a 15 s lease, renews every 5 s, and a 20 s GC pause freezes it. What happens on wake-up?
details.a: A standby took over after the lease expired, but the paused process still believes it leads. Without fencing both could write. Lease expiry gives liveness, not safety.

details.q: When should you avoid electing a leader?
details.a: When the work splits into independent pieces. One leader is a throughput and availability bottleneck and every election is downtime. Give each shard or hash bucket its own owner via [consistent hashing](#/sd/f/consistent-hashing) and elect only for things that must be done by exactly one node, like metadata or a global scheduler.

prompts.q: Compare three ways to elect a leader and say when you would pick each.
points: Consensus (Raft, etcd, ZooKeeper): strongest, majority and terms
Lease with CAS on a coordinator: simple, depends on the coordinator's consistency
ID or clock schemes break under partitions
Names the cost: election time is downtime

prompts.q: Explain split brain and how you prevent a deposed leader from doing damage.
points: Two nodes both believe they lead and accept writes
Deposed leader may not know (pause, partition)
Fencing token (term or epoch) checked by the resource
Majority decisions so two sides cannot both win

prompts.q: Does this system really need a leader? Argue for partitioning the work instead.
points: A leader is a bottleneck and a failure window
Partition by key with consistent hashing, one owner per piece
Keep a leader only for truly singleton jobs
